blocks.content: Direction problems test whether you can track a person's movement across multiple turns and calculate their final position or displacement from the starting point.  CGL asks 1–2 such questions per exam.

cells:
NORTH (N) SOUTH (S) EAST (E) WEST (W)

NORTH-EAST (NE) NORTH-WEST (NW) SOUTH-EAST (SE) SOUTH-WEST (SW)

KEY TURNING RULES:

Facing North → Turn Left → Now facing West

Facing North → Turn Right → Now facing East

Facing South → Turn Left → Now facing East

Facing South → Turn Right → Now facing West

Facing East → Turn Left → Now facing North

Facing East → Turn Right → Now facing South

Facing West → Turn Left → Now facing South

Facing West → Turn Right → Now facing North

Any direction → U-Turn (180°) → Opposite direction

When path forms a right angle: Displacement = √(horizontal² + vertical²)

Example: 3 km East + 4 km North → Displacement = √(3²+4²) = √(9+16) = √25 = 5 km

Common Pythagorean triplets: (3,4,5) | (5,12,13) | (8,15,17) | (7,24,25)

blocks.content: Ex.1 A person walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point?
Sol. N:5km → Turn right → E:3km → Turn right → S:5km. Net N-S: 5−5=0. Net E-W: 3 km East. Distance from start = 3 km East. Ans: 3 km
Ex.2 Facing North, Rahul walks 10 m, turns left 10 m, turns left 10 m. What direction is he facing now?
Sol. Start: North. Turn left → West. Turn left again → South. Ans: South
Ex.3 A man starts from point P, walks 4 km South, turns East walks 3 km. What is the straight-line distance from P?
Ex.4 Arjun walks 6 km North, then turns right and walks 4 km, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. How far is he from the start and in what direction?
Sol. N:6 → E:4 → S:6 → E:4. Net N-S: 6−6=0. Net E-W: 4+4=8 km East. Ans: 8 km East

cells:
Morning (before noon): Shadow falls towards WEST (sun rises in East)

Evening (after noon): Shadow falls towards EAST (sun sets in West)

12 noon: Shadow falls directly SOUTH in India (Northern hemisphere)

If shadow falls to the LEFT of a person → person is facing NORTH (morning)

If shadow falls to the RIGHT of a person → person is facing SOUTH (morning)

If shadow falls IN FRONT of a person → person is facing EAST (evening) / WEST (morning)

blocks.content: Ex.5 At 7 AM, Ravi's shadow falls to his right. Which direction is he facing?
Sol. Morning → sun in East → shadow falls West. Shadow to the right = West is to the right → facing South. Ans: South
Ex.6 During morning, two friends A and B are standing facing each other. A's shadow falls to his left. Which direction is B facing?
Sol. Morning shadow → West. A's shadow to his left means West is to his left → A faces North. B faces A, so B faces South. Ans: South
Q.29 Ram walks 10 m South, then 6 m East, then 10 m North. How far is he from start?
Ans: (b) 6 m Hint: N-S cancel (10S and 10N). Net = 6 m East. Distance = 6 m.
Q.30 A man facing West turns 90° clockwise. Which direction is he now facing?
Q.31 P walks 5 km West, turns South and walks 3 km. What is straight-line distance from start?
Q.32 In the morning, if a man's shadow falls behind him, in which direction is he walking?
Ans: (c) East Hint: Morning sun in East. Shadow behind = sun in front → facing East.
